Together we... "soar on wings like eagles, run and not grow weary, walk and not grow faint" Isaiah 40:31
Welcome to Coombe Bissett Church of England VA Primary School
At Coombe Bissett Primary School, we take pride in our reputation for providing a high quality education, where academic achievements are achieved in a happy and nurturing environment.
It is our aim that children come to school each day with a desire to learn, a smile on their face, and a motivation to do their very best. We hope that after a day of learning and fun with their friends the smile that they leave with is an even bigger one than the one they arrived with!
Our class sizes allow our pupils to receive levels of high quality, personalised attention that are more challenging to achieve in larger environments. The children benefit from a team of dedicated staff who are committed to helping each and every child fulfil their potential.
Good manners, high expectations, and a Christian ethos of respecting and caring for one another, all combine to make Coombe Bissett an exceptional school to which we are all proud to belong and where real learning happens.
We invite you to visit our school and see first-hand all that we have to offer. I look forward to meeting you and finding out more about your son or daughter.
We have limited places available in some year groups
Please contact the School Office on 01722 718380 for further information.
School Day times
Breakfast club:From 7.45am Morning session:8:35 am - 12pm Afternoon session:1pm - 3.15 pm After school club:Available until 5.30pm
What the children think
Coombe Bissett is a small village primary school with 4 mixed age classes nestled gently within the rolling countryside just outside of Salisbury.
We are a friendly, family-centred and happy community. Our children are at the heart of everything we do and are nurtured within a caring Christian ethos to become the best versions of themselves that they can be.
"The school is safe but also fun. There is always someone to talk to if you are sad or worried" Rose, Year 6
"School is so much fun, our learning is disguised, sometimes it is so much fun we don't even realise that we are learning!" Toby, Year 6
"Everyone is nice to each other and nobody is mean" Year 2 pupil
As part of Fir Class' Enquiry, 'What makes our school special?', they had their first ever go at making videos about our school. Here are some of their results.
I came for a tour yesterday afternoon, , and I just wanted to send an email to say how incredibly impressed I was. Please can you pass on my thanks to Mrs Haworth, it was wonderful to speak to her and I found our discussion on your new curriculum very inspiring. The biggest thank you needs to go to the pupils though. Their manners, confidence and attitudes were exemplary. I was incredibly impressed with their confidence in speaking to visitors and by how each one greeted Mrs Haworth on our tour with a smile. The Year 6 ambassadors that I spoke to need a special mention. Their confidence in speaking to me was very impressive and they did not stumble when I put them on the spot with a few questions. It is clear to see how happy everyone is at the school.
Relationships at all levels are strong and supportive, because the school's values are lived and breathed. There is a positive, restorative approach to behaviour, through which each individual is encouraged to 'walk' and to 'run' closely together. Staff are excellent role models for pupils by relating so positively towards each other. In turn, pupils’ care for each other, including older for younger, is kind and generous. The small school setting means that families and children are known to all staff. Parents say that the staff are full of warmth and ‘invested on an individual level’ with the pupils. This can be seen in the commitment and care seen in all interactions around the school.
There is a strong team ethos and the determination to ensure pupils are successful learners is palpable.

pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Vision
“Soar on wings like eagles,
Run and not grow weary,
Walk and not be faint.”
Here at Coombe Bissett, we believe that each and every child is unique and special. It is our aim to enable each and every child:
Care (love & service)
Commitment (friendship & respect)
Belief (trust & hope)
Bravery (courage & justice)
Brilliance (wisdom & truth)
These values reflect the core British values of: Democracy, Rule of Law, Individual Liberty, Tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs and Mutual Respect.

Clubs
At Coombe Bissett we offer a wide range of clubs.
Lunchtime Clubs
There are a range of clubs on offer at lunchtime including Construction Club, Homework Club, Timetable Rockstars and Cartoon Drawing. We also run Time to Talk sessions during various lunchtimes.
After School Clubs
We offer a range of after school clubs for children, examples of which are Lego, Art, Football, Choir, Ukulele. Most of our clubs are on the School Gateway App or contact the school office for more information - office@coombebissett.wilts.sch.uk.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care :: Coombe Bissett Primary School
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
We are proud to offer Wrap Around Care to support our families. As well as providing breakfast and tea, the children are encouraged to join in with a range of activities from supervised outdoor play to arts and crafts. There is always an opportunity to have fun with their friends whilst parents are reassured that their children are safely looked after.
What are the hours of Wrap Around Care?
Breakfast Club will run Monday to Friday 7.45am-8.40am
After School Club will be from 3.15pm-5.30pm Mon to Thurs and 3.15pm-4.30pm Friday
How much will it cost?
Wrap Around Care will be charged per session:
3.15-5.30pm: £10 (including food)
There will be a £1 per minute late charge for any child collected after 5.30pm.
Before making your first booking, you will need to complete a registration form. In the event where both parents use the provision independently of each other a registration form should be completed by both parents.
All bookings and payments will be made through the School Gateway app, not the school office,
Bookings need to be made in advance, to ensure an accurate register and suitable staff provision.
What if my plans change and I need to cancel a booking?
Bookings for Breakfast and Afterschool clubs can be made/cancelled or amended up to the day before for Breakfast club and up to 10am on the day of the booking for After School Club on the School Gateway app.
After these times charges will still apply if your child is unable to attend. The charge relates to the place being held and not the actual attendance.
My plans have changed and I will not be able to pick my child up at 3.15pm. Can they still go to Afterschool?
Up to 10am you can use the School Gateway app to book the session for your child, if there is space. If you have an emergency after 10am and are unable to collect your child at the usual school time and need to use After School Club please call the office.
I am running late for collection at the end of Afterschool, what shall I do?
All parents/carers are requested to make sure their child/children are collected by 5:30pm. If you are unavoidably delayed please telephone the Club on 07514019111 or email wac@coombebissett.wilts.sch.uk
When late collections after 5.30pm occur on more than three occasions we reserve the right to withdraw access to the club
What will my child do at Afterschool?
The aim is for the children to have fun in a safe and secure environment. They will have the opportunity to make, create, bake, play and have fun with friends from across the school.
All staff are fully paediatric first aid and Safeguarding trained and will follow the school’s related policies and procedures.
Will food be provided?
At Breakfast Club, a variety of different breakfast foods will be available on different days including cereals, yoghurts, fruit and brioches.
At the second session of Afterschool, food will be provided and will be generally bread based (sandwiches, wraps, spaghetti hoops on toast, pizza) alongside fruit and snacks.

pageCache.pageTitle: Online Safety :: Coombe Bissett Primary School
pageCache.text:
Online Safety
The progressive development of our children’s digital awareness and online safety is woven throughout our Computing curriculum and also forms a crucial part of our RSHE (Relationships Sex and Health Education) provision.
Our overarching intent is for our children to become “Digital Citizens” who can manage their digital identity effectively and ensure that all of their online behaviour is safe and positive.
At Coombe Bissett, we recognise that computing is an integral part of everyday life and will play an immeasurable part in our children’s futures and we appreciate the many benefits that it can bring to enhance learning.
We strive to provide our children with the skills, creativity and enthusiasm to live and thrive in a world increasingly dependent on online technology.
Therefore we explicitly teach our children how to use the internet in a secure and respectful way: about taking precautions and managing risks online and how to report anything that makes them feel uncomfortable; how to behave online as they would in “real life” (with kindness) etc.
Helping your child to navigate their online world
To help our parents feel more confident helping their child navigate the online world safely, we encourage them to complete the following online courses:
Annual Award for Online Safety 3-7 years
Annual Award for Online Safety 7-11 years
TV ad – Safety advice from a 10 year old.
Share Aware, from NSPCC and O2 resources recommend that parents and carers have regular and informed conversations with their child about online safety.
Their aim is to get every family in the UK chatting about their child’s online world, just like they would about their day at school:
“We tell children that’s it’s good to share, but online it’s different and sometimes it can be dangerous.”
O2 & NSPCC Online Safety Helpline – 0808 800 5002
In – game chat: A guide for parents and carers
The PEGI age rating on game packaging e.g. 3, 7, 12, 16, 18 means that the game shouldn’t be played by a young person under that age. Additional Consumer Information (ACI)Use the “Search” function to find a game and you’ll be shown a content breakdown including:
· How much graphic content appears in the game;
· How often/where it appears and how strong it is
Building up their Digital Resilience
Internet Matters features up-to-date resources e.g. a Digital Resilience Toolkit:
“Just like teaching a child to ride a bike or cross the road, digital resilience is another way to highlight the need to help children cope with whatever the online world throws at them.”
The best way to protect your child from cyberbullying is to take an active interest right from the start. They need your love and protection online as much as they do in the real world. What your child is exposed to will depend on how they’re using the internet. For example, social network users are more likely to experience cyberbullying, see sexual or violent images, or have contact with strangers.
How to protect your child from Cyberbullying
Managing social activity
UK Safer Internet Centre Responding to Sexting
The Government’s ThinkUKnow website has published some online activities for parents and carers to explore with their children at home in order to demonstrate the importance of staying safe online:
Ages 4-5 can be found here. Ages 5-7 can be found here. Ages 8-10 can be found here. Ages 11 and over can be found here.
Further resources include:

· CEOP Information about online safety and who to contact if you have concerns.

Parking
School Parking
Parking is a challenge for many schools, but we are very fortunate to have the use of the Village Hall Car Park. Every year we enter into an agreement where we rent the car park in exchange for a peppercorn.
Below is what we have agreed:
It’s important to note that the car park is owned by the Village Hall and we have been given permission to use it, if we break the rules then this privilege will be lost.
Please do not use the staff car park unless you have permission to do so, if you are late please use the Village Hall car park or Shutts Lane and walk your child/ren into school.
It’s a lot, we know, if you park with consideration and be mindful of others you cannot go wrong… unless you park on the grass verge!
Monday & Tuesday Parking
Every 2nd Monday of the month, the oldies lunch runs between 11 and 3 pm. Some village hall users will be driving others will be picked up through the course of the afternoon and the car park must remain clear for this to happen. The car park may not look very busy but those that are there would like to leave without getting blocked in. Do not enter the car park before 3pm.
On Tuesdays, there are multiple pilates classes back to back and their peak cross-over time is 2.45 pm. To prevent overcrowding we have agreed that parents will not enter the car park or park down Shutts Lane before 3 pm, if you arrive early please wait in the village until 3 pm. We have the use of the cricket field there is no need to arrive early to secure a parking spot, and we now have lots of room.
This is a new arrangement with CB Parish Council and we need to make sure we stick to the rules. This arrangement will be reviewed regularly and permission will be removed if we block parking for village hall users.
The cricket field will be opened at 3 pm, The Friends will send a message via Facebook to confirm it's okay to enter the car park. Below are the messages you should expect to see
1. Cricket field is open
2. The cricket field is open but wet so follow the parking plan - you won't get stuck this is about preventing a tricky area that does get churned up quickly.
3. The cricket field is closed - an alternative parking plan
4. Reminder of where not to park in the village and on Shutts Lane

Maths
At Coombe Bissett Primary School it is our intention to implement and deliver the Mathematics National Curriculum in an active and relevant way, which opens horizons and supports our vision and intent for the whole curriculum.
The intent of our mathematics curriculum is to design a curriculum, which is accessible to all and will maximise the development of every pupil’s ability and academic achievement. We deliver lessons that are creative and engaging using a mastery approach. The benefit of this approach is it caters for all styles of learners, ensures secure learning for higher attaining pupils and time and support for pupils that find Mathematics more challenging to keep up with their peers. We intend for pupils to make rich connections across mathematical ideas to develop fluency, mathematical reasoning and competence in solving increasingly sophisticated problems.
We intend for our pupils to be able to apply their mathematical knowledge to science and other subjects. We intend pupils to know that it is essential to everyday life, critical to science, technology and engineering, and necessary for financial literacy and most forms of employment. As our pupils progress, we intend for our pupils to be able to understand the world, have the ability to reason mathematically, have an appreciation of the beauty and power of mathematics, and a sense of enjoyment and curiosity about the subject.
